label: neiso 105 fossil offer
definition: KEEPER. neiso-105 is a full-span 2023/2024/2025 replay of the superseded keeper's (2026-08-17-neiso-99-joint-p1) recipe with EXACTLY ONE delta: a single scalar 0.93391 (a 6.609% cut) applied to 12 markup bands of offer_curve_by_group -- committed/econ_low/econ_high of CC_REGULAR, CC_CHP, CT_PEAKER, ST_GAS. All four peak bands, every phys_*, econ_low_share, pct_peaking, and the declared-neutral CT_CHP group are unchanged. Applied through the rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 13 [R-MEASURED] authorized price-tuning channel on owner direction 2026-09-06 ('shift the fossil offer curves down, preserving the ratio'): ONE config across every scored year, declared ex ante in PREREG-neiso105-offer-level-resized-2026-09-06.md before the solve, never swept against the gates. Sizing: the cut is the PREREG-neiso104 in-sample geometric-mean price-bias target (+3.4678%, fixed before either arm solved and never moved) divided by the neiso-104 screen's measured pass-through coefficient (0.5247) -- 0.034678 / 0.5247 = 6.609%. Ledgered as a free parameter under rule 21 [R-DOF] (owner ruling R-AY, 2026-09-06): identification source is the ruling itself, not a measured input, reported at full magnitude. Headline effect, C3a mean LMP bias: +3.13% -> -3.36% (2023), +5.66% -> -0.02% (2024), +1.65% -> -1.89% (2025); mean absolute error 3.48% -> 1.76%. REPORTED AGAINST INTEREST, not hidden: the realized full-span pass-through turned out to be 0.764, not the 0.5247 the cut was sized on -- the neiso-104 screen year (2025) is the lowest-pass-through year in the record -- so the in-sample bias OVERSHOOTS, from +3.47% under the incumbent to -1.77% here. The scalar was deliberately NOT resized after the fact (PREREG-neiso105 section 3 pre-committed it would not be raised, and it is equally not lowered, a second time). DETERMINATION CALIBRATED: 0 FAILs; C3c price tail/scarcity is the sole ledgered caveat, carried forward unchanged in substance from the incumbent keeper (rubric v3.3 non-downgrading); C1, C2, C3a, C3b, C4, C6, C8 all PASS. Bundle results/calibration/neiso105_offerlevel. Lineage: PREREG-neiso104-fossil-offer-level-2026-09-06.md, ADDENDUM-neiso104-gdrift-2026-09-06.md, FINDING-neiso104-offer-level-screen-2026-09-06.md, ADDENDUM-neiso104-env-correction-2026-09-06.md, PREREG-neiso105-offer-level-resized-2026-09-06.md.
market_story: CC_REGULAR, CC_CHP, CT_PEAKER and ST_GAS -- New England's fossil merit stack -- were priced too rich against realized LMP under the incumbent recipe (mean absolute bias 3.48% across 2023-2025); this run does not add a price adder, it takes a small, declared cut off the SAME merit-order markup bands the fleet already carries, leaving physics (phys_*), the econ/must-run split (econ_low_share) and the peaking share (pct_peaking) untouched. Because the cut is uniform across bands and years, the merit order and forced-energy structure are unchanged in kind -- only the price level the stack clears at moves down. The cut was sized off 2025's measured pass-through, the lowest of the three years, so applying the same scalar to 2023 and 2024 (whose pass-through is higher, 0.953 and 0.814) over-corrects them: all three years now sit on the opposite side of zero from before (2023 +3.13% -> -3.36%, 2024 +5.66% -> -0.02%, 2025 +1.65% -> -1.89%), but the swing is smaller than the bias it replaced, so mean absolute error still falls to 1.76%.
